skill.name: python-design-patterns
skill.description: Python design patterns including KISS, Separation of Concerns, Single Responsibility, and composition over inheritance. Use when making architecture decisions, refactoring code structure, or evaluating when abstractions are appropriate.
skill.summary: Guides Python architecture and refactoring decisions with simple, testable design patterns.
skill.author: wshobson

content.value_statement: Python projects often grow complex when responsibilities mix and abstractions appear too early. This skill guides focused refactors using KISS, SRP, layering, composition, and dependency injection.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to keep Python code simple instead of adding factories or registries.
Separates HTTP, business logic, repository, and response formatting responsibilities.
Compares inheritance with composition for testable service design.
Uses the Rule of Three to avoid premature abstraction.
Suggests dependency injection patterns with protocols and fake implementations.
limitations: Does not execute or validate Python code.
Does not provide framework-specific architecture rules for every Python web stack.
Does not replace domain modeling or product requirements analysis.
Uses illustrative examples that require adaptation before production use.

use_cases.title: Untangle a Handler
use_cases.description: Split a large request handler into validation, service, repository, and response responsibilities.

use_cases.title: Review an Abstraction
use_cases.description: Decide whether a factory, registry, base class, or protocol is justified by current requirements.

use_cases.title: Teach Maintainable Python
use_cases.description: Show concrete examples of KISS, SRP, composition, and dependency injection during code review.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Simple Module
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-design-patterns to review this Python module for KISS and single responsibility. Identify the smallest useful refactor and explain why.

prompt_templates.title: Split Mixed Responsibilities
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-design-patterns to separate HTTP parsing, validation, business logic, persistence, and response formatting in this code.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Composition or Inheritance
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-design-patterns to decide whether this design should use inheritance, composition, protocols, or constructor injection.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Layered Refactor
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-design-patterns to propose a staged refactor plan for this Python service. Apply KISS, Rule of Three, layering, and dependency injection.

output_examples.input: Review a user handler that validates requests, writes database rows, and formats responses.
output_examples.output: The handler has at least three reasons to change. Move business rules into a service, database access into a repository, and keep response formatting in the handler.

output_examples.input: Decide whether two similar processing functions need a shared abstraction.
output_examples.output: Do not abstract yet. The examples have different validation and error behavior, so a shared helper would hide important differences.

output_examples.input: Improve a notification service that directly creates its SMTP dependency.
output_examples.output: Inject a sender dependency through the constructor. This keeps notification rules separate from delivery setup and makes tests easier.

best_practices: Start with the simplest design that satisfies current requirements.
Separate code by reason to change, not by pattern name.
Use dependency injection when it improves testing or replaces hardcoded infrastructure.
anti_patterns: Adding factories, registries, or base classes before repeated needs exist.
Mixing request parsing, business rules, database access, and response formatting.
Using inheritance to share behavior when composition would be clearer.

faq.question: What design principles does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers KISS, single responsibility, separation of concerns, composition, Rule of Three, function size, and dependency injection.

faq.question: Can it rewrite my whole application?
faq.answer: It can guide a refactor plan, but you still need to apply and test changes in your codebase.

faq.question: Does it prefer patterns over simple code?
faq.answer: No. The skill favors simple code and recommends patterns only when they solve a clear problem.

faq.question: Is it useful for code review?
faq.answer: Yes. It helps reviewers explain coupling, mixed responsibilities, premature abstraction, and testability concerns.

faq.question: Does it depend on a specific Python framework?
faq.answer: No. The examples are general and can be adapted to web services, workers, libraries, and internal tools.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
